The first is the multiplication-by-a-homogeneous-polynomial step in the filtration argument, found in InitProp.mul_of_isHomogeneous and in the hsum block of exists_fg_le_and_forall_le_sup_pow. The second is the flat + IsLocalHom + FaithfullyFlat construction, found in iInf_sup_pow_le and main. findings.problem: The same filtration-degree argument is proved twice. If C is homogeneous of degree i, its evaluation lies in 𝔪^i, and multiplying it by an element of I ⊔ 𝔪^(k+1) lands in I ⊔ 𝔪^(i+k+1). The proof is the same in both places. Split the element via mem_sup, use mul_add, put the I-part in via mul_mem_left and add_mem_sup, get eval C ∈ 𝔪^i from eval_mem_span_pow_of_isHomogeneous (rewriting with h𝔪), multiply with mul_mem_mul, then fix the exponent with ← pow_add / convert / omega. Lines 121-130 do this for C' * P, and lines 268-281 do it for H p * F p, so the block is open-coded twice with only the names changed.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma before InitProp, in the Criterion section:

lemma eval_mul_mem_sup_pow (h𝔪 : Ideal.span (Set.range t) = 𝔪) {C : MvPolynomial σ A} {i k : ℕ} (hC : C.IsHomogeneous i) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ I ⊔ 𝔪 ^ (k + 1)) : eval t C * x ∈ I ⊔ 𝔪 ^ (i + k + 1)

Proof sketch: obtain ⟨y, hy, z, hz, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hx. Then rewrite with mul_add, use add_mem_sup (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hy), and for the second part combine eval_mem_span_pow_of_isHomogeneous (after rw ← h𝔪) with hz via Ideal.mul_mem_mul. Finish with pow_add and an exponent rewrite.

Use 1 (InitProp.mul_of_isHomogeneous): after rw [map_mul], apply `have := eval_mul_mem_sup_pow h𝔪 hC'h hPev`, which has k = n - i, and then rewrite i + (n - i) + 1 = n + 1 with `Nat.add_sub_cancel' hin`.

Use 2 (hsum): after rw [map_sum] and Submodule.sum_mem, `rw [map_mul]` and apply the lemma to hHh p and `(by rw [hFev p hpT]; exact Submodule.add_mem_sup (Ideal.subset_span ⟨p, hpT, rfl⟩) (hm'𝔪 p hpT) : eval t (F p) ∈ J ⊔ 𝔪^(p.2+1))` (with J as the ideal I of the lemma). Then rewrite the exponent with Nat.sub_add_cancel hp2. This replaces the hHev/mul_add/convert block.

findings.problem: The proof that A is faithfully flat over each S i is written out twice. In iInf_sup_pow_le (lines 472-475) it is flat_of_tower, then IsLocalHom from isUnit_coe_iff with a hand-built hle (`fun i j h => (hmax h).le`), then FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom. In main (lines 510-518, the `hff` block) the same three steps appear again, with the same `hle` derived from hmax. The `hle` derivation from `hmax` is also repeated in map_maximalIdeal_eq (lines 424-426). This is the key structural fact of the tower and it is proved by copy-paste.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma after isUnit_coe_iff:

lemma faithfullyFlat_of_tower [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] (hcov : ∀ x : A, ∃ i, x ∈ S i) (hflat : ∀ ⦃i j : ι⦄ (h : i ≤ j), (Subring.inclusion (hS h)).Flat) (hmax : ∀ ⦃i j : ι⦄ (h : i ≤ j), Ideal.map (Subring.inclusion (hS h)) (maximalIdeal (S i)) = maximalIdeal (S j)) (i : ι) : Module.FaithfullyFlat (S i) A

Proof: haveI := flat_of_tower S hS hcov hflat i. Build IsLocalHom (algebraMap (S i) A) from `(isUnit_coe_iff S hS hcov (fun _ _ h => (hmax h).le) y).mp`, then `exact Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom`. This is a verbatim lift of the main block, and it is applicable because both call sites already have the same hypotheses.

In iInf_sup_pow_le, replace lines 472-475 by `haveI := faithfullyFlat_of_tower S hS hcov hflat hmax j` (the Flat instance is not needed afterwards). In main, replace the whole hff block by `fun i => faithfullyFlat_of_tower S hS hcov hflat hmax i`.
findings.benefit: The faithful-flatness of A over S i becomes a named, reusable result instead of a five-line instance setup duplicated in two proofs. The local `hle` in main shrinks away for this purpose, and a reader sees the theorem's second conclusion directly. This also keeps the two uses from drifting apart.
